# Sanity

> Sanity is the Content Operating System for the AI era. It gives teams a structured content backbone (Content Lake), a fully customizable editing environment (Sanity Studio), and APIs that power everything from websites to AI agents. Model content around how your business actually works, automate the repetitive stuff, and deliver to any channel from a single source of truth.

## Glossary

- [Glossary](https://www.sanity.io/glossary): Explore definitions and explanations for terms relating to the world of CMSes and Sanity. Let this be your guide to the content management world.
- [AI gateway definition](https://www.sanity.io/glossary/ai-gateway): An AI gateway sits between your app and many model providers, offering one API and account. How it works, how it differs from an API gateway, and the trade-offs
- [API gateway definition](https://www.sanity.io/glossary/api-gateway): An API gateway is the front door between client applications and backend services, handling routing, authorization, monitoring, and traffic management.
- [API rate limiting definition](https://www.sanity.io/glossary/api-rate-limiting): API rate limiting caps how many requests a client can make in a time window. Learn how 429 responses, token buckets, quotas, and concurrency limits differ.
- [API versioning definition](https://www.sanity.io/glossary/api-versioning): API versioning publishes an API in parallel, labeled editions so changes reach clients on their own schedule. Compare URI, header, semantic, and date-based API
- [API-First definition](https://www.sanity.io/glossary/api-first): API-First is a development approach that defines the API contract before any code is written. What it means, its benefits, and how agents consume it.
- [Astro overview](https://www.sanity.io/glossary/astro): Astro is a server-first web framework for content-rich sites, with client and server islands, the Content Layer API, and a Sanity integration.

- [Composability definition](https://www.sanity.io/glossary/composability): Composability is an architecture of interchangeable components. How it works, how to implement it, and how it now underpins API and agent integration.
